newsitem.title: ALBANIA: First wave of Italian troops arrive in Albania.
newsitem.headline: First wave of Italian troops arrive in Albania.

text.p: The first wave of Italian troops leading a multinational security mission to Albania arrived early on Friday.
An Italian naval vessel, the Pantellaria, carrying an army advance unit and escorted by a small Italian gunboat, the Rimini, steamed into the Albanian port of Durres shortly after 8 a.m. (0600 GMT).

An Italian military transport plane carrying about two dozen paratroopers landed at Tirana airport less than an hour later. Two more Italian military aircraft landed shortly after 10 a.m.(0800 GMT). All three were Lockheed C130 Hercules aircraft that had flown from Pisa.

The troops included a contingent of special forces with orders to secure the airport perimeter and a group of specialists whose job is to ensure the airport can operate around the clock and not just during daylight hours as at present.
The efficient running of the airport is vital as it will be used for further troop arrivals as well as aid shipments, Italian military sources said.
The gunboat Rimini returned to Italy shortly after making an inspection of the waters around Durres.

"Our mission does not rule out risks, but we hope the Albanian people will understand that we are here to help them," said Colonel Enrico Nardi, commander of the Italian landing unit in Durres. "We plan to check the road between Durres and Tirana and perhaps the airport."
Journalists at the airport and in the port city of Durres 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana said there were no incidents as the first combat-ready foreign troops stationed to Albania arrived.
The Italian troops are spearheading a 6,000-strong multinational force which will protect aid convoys.

The Pantelleria was carrying troops from the Italian army's 9th regiment as well as about 20 men from an Italian pioneer regiment and a number of marines. It left the Italian port of Brindisi on Thursday evening.
Journalists in Durres said the troops began disembarking shortly after the ship arrived and two armoured vehicles were also unloaded.
The task of the army advance unit is to inspect the area where the main landing will take place and reconnoitre the road from Durres to the capital Tirana, military sources in Rome said.
The bulk of the multinational force, the first of its kind led by Italy, is due to begin deploying next Monday to protect and to assist in the delivery of relief aid to Albania.
The soldiers were given a special guide to the country which included useful Albanian phrases such as "Drop the gun!"

Troops from France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are also in the force. It has U.N. Security Council approval but is being organised by a so-called "coalition of willing" nations. Austria and Denmark are also considering participation.
More than 200 people have been killed since rebels took control of the south last month in an eruption of anger following the collapse of a number of pyramid savings schemes.
Thousands of small arms looted from abandoned weapons depots are still on the streets but the multinational force has no mandate to recover them.
The first French troops to join the international force sailed from the southern port of Toulon on Friday.
Some 350 soldiers of the 9th Paratroop infantry division, the first part of a 1,000-strong French contingent, began a three-day voyage to Durres on the landing ship Orage.
